Make curl downloads in docker pkg-resolver scripts fail on HTTP errors and retry
comments:
cxzl25 opened a new pull request, #8963:
URL: https://github.com/apache/hadoop/pull/8963

   ### Description of PR
   The docker image used by Yetus precommit fails to build from time to time while downloading third-party artifacts. For example, the build failed with:
   ```
       RUN pkg-resolver/install-spotbugs.sh ubuntu:noble
       gzip: stdin: not in gzip format
       tar: Error is not recoverable: exiting now
   ```
   
   The `dev-support/docker/pkg-resolver/*.sh` scripts call `curl` without `-f`. On an HTTP error, curl exits 0 and writes the error page into the archive, so the build only fails later in `tar` and the real cause is hidden. The scripts also never retry transient failures.
   
   This PR changes every curl download in these scripts (maven, spotbugs, boost,
   protobuf/abseil, hadolint, isa-l, nodejs, epel, yasm) to:
   ```
       curl -f -L -s -S --retry 5 --retry-delay 5 ...
   ```
   
   - `-f`: fail at the download step on HTTP errors and print the status code.
   - `--retry 5 --retry-delay 5`: retry transient errors (timeouts, HTTP 408/429/5xx)
     up to 5 times, 5 seconds apart.
   - `install-boost.sh`: changed from `curl -L ... > file` to the same `-s -S ... -o file`
     form as the other scripts.
   
   ### How was this patch tested?
   GHA

summary: Defensive copies and immutability fixes for hadoop-distcp SpotBugs warnings
description:
The nightly trunk build (qbt) reports 19 SpotBugs warning(s) in hadoop-tools/hadoop-distcp. This issue tracks fixing 10 of them by code changes (defensive copies, unmodifiable views and related small behaviour changes), with unit tests:

# SimpleCopyListing, SS_SHOULD_BE_STATIC on maxRetries: private static final int MAX_RETRIES
# DiffInfo, CT_CONSTRUCTOR_THROW: package-private class made final
# DynamicInputChunk, CT_CONSTRUCTOR_THROW: package-private class made final
# DynamicInputChunkContext, CT_CONSTRUCTOR_THROW: package-private class made final
# CopyListingFileStatus, EI_EXPOSE_REP2 on setAclEntries: copies the list, keeping null as null
# CopyListingFileStatus, EI_EXPOSE_REP2 on setXAttrs: copies into a LinkedHashMap, keeping null as null and the iteration order
# DistCpContext, EI_EXPOSE_REP2 on setSourcePaths: copies the list, keeping null as null
# DistCpContext, EI_EXPOSE_REP on getSourcePaths: returns an unmodifiable view, or null
# DistCpOptions$Builder, EI_EXPOSE_REP2 on <init>: copies the source path list (DistCpOptions is documented as immutable)
# DistCpOptionSwitch, EI_EXPOSE_REP on getOption: returns a clone of the enum's shared CLI Option

No public method signature changes.

The remaining 9 warnings, where the current behaviour is intended, are handled by narrow module-level SpotBugs exclusions tracked in HADOOP-20017.

Contains content generated by Claude Code.

   ### Description of PR
   
   JIRA: [HADOOP-20088](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HADOOP-20088)
   
   This PR fixes by code 10 of the 19 SpotBugs warnings that the nightly qbt builds (JDK 17 and JDK 21) report in `hadoop-tools/hadoop-distcp`. It is the code half of the solution; the other half (narrow module-level exclusions for the 9 warnings whose behaviour is intended) is in [HADOOP-20017](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HADOOP-20017) / PR #8818, following the review feedback there.
   
   | # | Class | Warning | Resolution |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | 1 | `SimpleCopyListing` | SS_SHOULD_BE_STATIC `maxRetries` | `private static final int MAX_RETRIES = 3` |
   | 2 | `DiffInfo` | CT_CONSTRUCTOR_THROW `<init>` | package-private class made `final` |
   | 3 | `DynamicInputChunk` | CT_CONSTRUCTOR_THROW `<init>` | package-private class made `final` |
   | 4 | `DynamicInputChunkContext` | CT_CONSTRUCTOR_THROW `<init>` | package-private class made `final` |
   | 5 | `CopyListingFileStatus` | EI_EXPOSE_REP2 `setAclEntries` | copies the list, keeping null as null |
   | 6 | `CopyListingFileStatus` | EI_EXPOSE_REP2 `setXAttrs` | copies into a `LinkedHashMap`, keeping null as null and the iteration order |
   | 7 | `DistCpContext` | EI_EXPOSE_REP2 `setSourcePaths` | copies the list, keeping null as null |
   | 8 | `DistCpContext` | EI_EXPOSE_REP `getSourcePaths` | returns an unmodifiable view, or null |
   | 9 | `DistCpOptions$Builder` | EI_EXPOSE_REP2 `<init>` | copies the source path list. `DistCpOptions` is documented as immutable, and `getSourcePaths()` already returns an unmodifiable copy |
   | 10 | `DistCpOptionSwitch` | EI_EXPOSE_REP `getOption` | returns a clone of the enum's shared, JVM-wide CLI `Option`. The only caller is `OptionsParser`, which just adds it to `Options` |

summary: Import jetty-bom in hadoop-project for consistent Jetty dependency versions
description:
hadoop-project lists several Jetty artifacts in dependencyManagement while transitive Jetty modules (jetty-http, jetty-security, etc.) can resolve to different versions than jetty-server.

Import org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-bom (${jetty.version}) in the parent POM, matching the approach used in Apache Ozone. Remove redundant Jetty entries without exclusions from dependencyManagement, and drop the duplicate jetty-bom import from hadoop-yarn-applications-catalog-webapp.

Precedent: https://github.com/apache/ozone/blob/c359bf72ea6aa98147fd1935952c805242f1d18c/pom.xml#L265-L271

jojochuang opened a new pull request, #8979:
URL: https://github.com/apache/hadoop/pull/8979

   ### Description of PR
   
   Import `org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-bom` in `hadoop-project` `dependencyManagement` so transitive Jetty artifacts (for example `jetty-http` and `jetty-security`) align with `${jetty.version}` instead of versions declared inside each Jetty POM.
   
   Remove redundant managed Jetty coordinates that only repeated the version (`jetty-util`, `jetty-servlet`, `jetty-webapp`, `websocket-client`, `jetty-servlet-tester`). Keep `jetty-server` and `javax-websocket-server-impl` entries that apply exclusions.
   
   Remove the duplicate `jetty-bom` import and redundant explicit versions on `org.eclipse.jetty.http2` dependencies in `hadoop-yarn-applications-catalog-webapp` now that the parent BOM applies.
   
   Same approach as [Apache Ozone](https://github.com/apache/ozone/blob/c359bf72ea6aa98147fd1935952c805242f1d18c/pom.xml#L265-L271).
   
   [HADOOP-20081](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HADOOP-20081)

   @adoroszlai You're right: **today**, on 9.4, the BOM import is equivalent to the explicit entries and adds no dependency. My concern is what it does at HADOOP-19972, when ${jetty.version} moves to 12.1.x.
   
   jetty-bom 12.1 manages none of the servlet-stack coordinates this PR un-manages: in Jetty 12 they move to org.eclipse.jetty.ee8:* (jetty-ee8-servlet, jetty-ee8-webapp, jetty-ee8-websocket-javax-server), which live in a separate jetty-ee8-bom this PR does not import. The only servlet/webapp coordinate the 12 BOM does manage is org.eclipse.jetty.ee:jetty-ee-webapp — the jakarta environment, which HADOOP-19912 explicitly rejects in favor of ee8 (javax.servlet).
   
   So at the 19972 bump the BOM silently stops managing the servlet stack and manages the wrong environment instead. Nothing fails at that moment — the port has to notice, add jetty-ee8-bom, and rewrite every renamed coordinate. With explicit entries those decisions are one visible diff in hadoop-project/pom.xml; **with the BOM they can be skipped and rediscovered later.** That's the whole objection: the 19972 port should have to make these decisions in review, not inherit them silently from a BOM's contents.
   
   If the BOM is wanted, I'd support importing jetty-bom + jetty-ee8-bom together after 19972 lands, against final coordinates. Until then: keep the explicit entries, land #8894 first (approved, queued in the HADOOP-19912 merge order, edits this same dependencyManagement block), and attach HADOOP-20081 to HADOOP-19912 so the sequencing is visible.

summary: ChecksumFileSystem.readVectored leaks buffers allocated through caller's IntFunction allocator
comments:
[~stevel@apache.org] this may interest you
iemejia opened a new pull request, #8511:
URL: https://github.com/apache/hadoop/pull/8511

   ## Description
   
   `ChecksumFileSystem.readVectored()` allocates buffers for both data ranges and checksum ranges through the caller's allocator (`IntFunction<ByteBuffer>`). After checksum verification completes, the checksum buffers were never released because:
   
   1. The caller has no reference to checksum buffers (only data range results are visible)
   2. The system did not call the `release` consumer on them
   
   This causes buffer leaks when callers use a tracking or pooled allocator. This bug was discovered while working on Apache Parquet's `TrackingByteBufferAllocator`, which detected unreleased buffers accumulating during vectored reads through `ChecksumFileSystem`.
   
   ## Root Cause
   
   In `ChecksumFileSystem.ChecksumFSInputChecker.readVectored()`, checksum ranges are read via `sums.readVectored(checksumRanges, allocate, release)`. The checksum buffers are used in `thenCombineAsync` calls for verification, but after verification completes, no code released them back to the caller's pool.
   
   A single checksum range can cover multiple data ranges, so the checksum buffer is shared across multiple `thenCombineAsync` calls — it must only be released once, after ALL verifications using it are complete.
   
   ## Fix
   
   After collecting all verification futures for a checksum range, use `CompletableFuture.allOf(verifications).thenRun(...)` to release the checksum buffer exactly once after all verifications complete:
   
   ```java
   CompletableFuture.allOf(verifications.toArray(new CompletableFuture[0]))
       .thenRun(() -> release.accept(checksumRange.getData().join()));
   ```
   
   This ensures:
   - Exactly-once release (not once per data range that shares the checksum buffer)
   - Release happens only after the buffer is no longer in use
   - Works correctly with both the 2-arg API (no-op release) and the 3-arg API
   
   ## Testing
   
   Added `testChecksumBuffersReleasedAfterVectoredRead()` to `TestLocalFSContractVectoredRead`:
   - Uses a counting allocator/release pair to track buffer lifecycle
   - Performs a vectored read through `LocalFileSystem` (which uses `ChecksumFileSystem`)
   - Asserts that the system calls the release consumer at least once for internal buffers
   - Confirmed the test **fails without the fix** (0 system-initiated releases) and **passes with it**
   
   All 54 existing vectored read contract tests continue to pass.
   
   ## JIRA
   
   https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HADOOP-19901

summary: Allow to skip recursive file deletion for non-empty directory
description:
A non-empty directory, as well as a directory where its emptiness is unknown, is deleted by listing all contained files (or objects with matching key prefix), then deleting those files (objects) in bulk delete requests, and finally deleting the (then) empty directory itself.

The recursive deletion of objects is not needed for S3 endpoints that support deleting non-empty directories (or path prefixes).

For example: The [VAST S3 endpoint supports deleting non-empty directories|https://kb.vastdata.com/documentation/docs/using-trash-folder-for-s3-objects-6] with a single request. Such a feature can only be fully leveraged if {{hadoop-aws}} coupd skip the recursive deletion.

   Fixes HADOOP-19801

   ### Description of PR
   The IPC `Server` currently enforces a hard upper limit on RPC request size via `ipc.maximum.data.length` (default 128 MB). Requests that exceed this limit are rejected immediately. However, requests that are abnormally large but still within the limit pass through silently, potentially causing GC pressure and cascading failures before any operator is aware.

summary: Pin Visual Studio, Git, vcpkg and Python in the Windows build image by version and hash
description:
{{dev-support/docker/Dockerfile_windows_10}} pins the JDK, Maven, CMake, zstd and MSYS2 downloads by SHA-512, but the rest of the image is not pinned:
* Visual Studio Build Tools come from the {{aka.ms/vs/16/release}} bootstrapper, which installs whatever 16.11 release is newest when the image is built.
* Git comes from Chocolatey: the image runs {{chocolatey.org/install.ps1}} unpinned, then {{choco install git.install}}, which takes whichever Git for Windows release the package currently names.
* vcpkg is checked out by tag, and {{bootstrap-vcpkg.bat}} downloads {{vcpkg.exe}} through a helper that checks only that the file carries a trusted signature, not whose.
* {{install-python.ps1}} does not check the installer's hash, and {{pip install python-dateutil}} takes the newest release: 4.0.0 since 1 November (plus its new dependency tzdata), not the 2.8.1 that the Linux images use.

Some install steps also pass when they fail: {{install-python.ps1}} and {{install-pip.ps1}} exit 0 when a download fails, and the exit code of the Visual C++ 2010 redistributable's installer is not checked. And {{rsync.exe}} imports {{msys-popt-0.dll}}, which neither Git for Windows nor the image provides.

This change:
* Visual Studio Build Tools: the fixed-version bootstrapper for 16.11.62, which installs that release, with a SHA-512 check.
* Git: PortableGit 2.56.0.4, with a SHA-512 check, extracted to {{C:\Git}}, the path the Jenkins Windows job and BUILDING.txt already use. This replaces Chocolatey and git.install. The step checks that PortableGit's post-install script ran, and sets {{http.sslBackend}} and {{credential.helper}} as git.install did.
* vcpkg: checked out by commit (the one the 2026.07.29 tag names, which is also the manifest's builtin-baseline), with {{vcpkg.exe}} downloaded directly and checked by SHA-512.
* Python: a SHA-512 check for the installer. {{install-python.ps1}} and {{install-pip.ps1}} stop on any failure and check the installed versions, and get-pip no longer adds the unpinned {{wheel}} package. pip installs python-dateutil 2.8.1 and six 1.17.0 from a requirements file with hashes ({{\--require-hashes}}, {{\--no-deps}}), then runs {{pip check}}.
* rsync: add MSYS2's popt, which provides {{msys-popt-0.dll}}, and check that {{rsync.exe}} starts. Stop copying MSYS2's libopenssl 3.5.2 and libzstd DLLs over the ones Git for Windows ships (OpenSSL 3.5.9, and an identical zstd).
* Download, check, install, verify and clean up each tool in one RUN, so no installer or archive stays in a lower layer, and check the exit codes of the Visual Studio, JDK and Visual C++ 2010 installers.
* Set PATH once, for all users, instead of seven per-user {{setx}} calls.
* Copy only the Python scripts and the requirements file from {{pkg-resolver}}, so changes to the Linux scripts there no longer invalidate the Windows image's later layers.
* BUILDING.txt: the image is now about 14 GB.

Every version chosen is at least 7 days old, as SECURITY.md's cooldown requires ({{.github/dependabot.yml}} uses 7 days). Git for Windows 2.56.1, a security release, qualifies on 17 November; the pull request will move to it then.

*Testing*
[Fork run 43631843328|https://github.com/GauthamBanasandra/hadoop/actions/runs/43631843328] tested this change on top of HADOOP-20087, with the trial GitHub Actions workflow in my fork that is not part of this change. The pull request links a run of its final version. Sizes are in decimal GB; the run summaries print GiB.
* The default (ltsc2022) image built on windows-2022 in 39 minutes: 14.4 GB, 5.8 GB compressed, down from 16.9 GB and 6.6 GB with HADOOP-20087 alone. As the build user, the image has Visual Studio 16.11.62, git 2.56.0.windows.4 and rsync 3.5.1 (which starts), and pip lists only pip 24.0, setuptools 65.5.1, python-dateutil 2.8.1 and six 1.17.0, with {{pip check}} passing. Nothing is left in {{C:\}} or {{C:\ProgramData}} apart from the installed tools.
* The ltsc2019 image, the Jenkins path, built under Hyper-V on windows-2022 (10.0.17763.9488): 14.2 GB, down from 16.0 GB. Its entry point, rsync and {{pip check}} ran.
* Full {{\-Pnative-win}} builds and the native smoke test passed on windows-2022 and windows-2025 under process isolation and on windows-2022 under Hyper-V isolation. The Windows-specific unit tests passed on windows-2022: 12 classes, 275 tests, no failures, 33 skipped, with the same six methods excluded as for HADOOP-20087.

summary: Pin the Windows build image's base to ltsc2022 and slim it for CI
description:
{{dev-support/docker/Dockerfile_windows_10}} builds from {{servercore:ltsc2019}} by tag, and the tag moves with every monthly update. GitHub's windows-2022 and windows-2025 runners can run ltsc2019 only under Hyper-V isolation. In fork runs, Hyper-V isolation made the Maven build 1.07x to 1.46x slower than process isolation, depending on the runner's VM type (measured by forcing Hyper-V on the ltsc2022 image). This change prepares the image for a GitHub Actions Windows build (HADOOP-19857):

* Make the base a build argument, defaulting to {{servercore:ltsc2022}} pinned by digest, so the default base changes only when the Dockerfile does. The pin is 10.0.20348.5761 (October), the base that the fork runs below tested. The Dockerfile notes to bump the digest monthly, no sooner than 7 days after Microsoft publishes the image (SECURITY.md requires a cooldown; {{.github/dependabot.yml}} uses 7 days).
* Check that the Visual Studio Build Tools install worked: {{vcvars64.bat}} runs, {{cl.exe}} is found and Windows SDK 10.0.19041 is present. Today the install step passes even when the installer fails: {{start /w}} reports success to {{||}} whatever the installer returns (it only sets {{%ERRORLEVEL%}}), so its {{IF "%ERRORLEVEL%"=="3010"}} test never runs.
* Delete vcpkg's build trees, downloads and packages in the same layer as the install, and turn off its binary cache, which kept a second copy of every package. On windows-2022 with the ltsc2022 base, the image shrinks from about 24.4 GB to 16.9 GB, and from about 8.8 GB to 6.6 GB compressed. Recent runs of the Jenkins Windows nightly {{hadoop-qbt-trunk-java8-win10-x86_64}} (#1471, #1477 to #1479) failed in {{docker build}} with "There is not enough space on the disk"; #1479 ran out while writing vcpkg's build trees into the image layer.
* Create {{C:\tmp}}, writable by the Users group. Tests that use {{file:///tmp}} resolve it to {{C:\tmp}}; on a host without it, {{TestPathData#testWithStringAndConfForBuggyPath}} fails, as it did in a fork run.
* {{dev-support/bin/hadoop.sh}} passes {{\-Dcmake.prefix.path}} on Windows, but hadoop-hdfs-native-client reads {{windows.cmake.prefix.path}}. Pass the property it reads. This affects only the Yetus build that the Jenkins Windows jobs run, and matches what BUILDING.txt documents.
* Stop changes to the Windows Dockerfile and {{dev-support/docker/vcpkg}} from rebuilding the Linux image caches (the {{build_image_cache.yml}} path filter). No Linux Dockerfile reads them.
* Update the Windows section of BUILDING.txt: which hosts need the ltsc2019 build argument, Docker Engine on Windows Server, which isolation to use on client and server hosts, when {{\-m 8g}} is needed, and the expected image size (about 17 GB, was 23 GB).

*Behaviour change*
Building without the {{WINDOWS_BASE_IMAGE}} build argument now needs a Windows 11 or Windows Server 2022 (or newer) host. Windows 10 and Windows Server 2019 hosts pass {{\--build-arg WINDOWS_BASE_IMAGE=mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2019}} and keep following that tag, as before; {{dev-support/jenkinsfile-windows-10}} now passes it. The Jenkins nightly {{hadoop-qbt-trunk-java8-win10-x86_64}} keeps its pipeline script in the job configuration rather than reading that file, so someone with access to the job needs to add the same argument to its {{docker build}} before this change is merged, or the nightly will switch to the ltsc2022 base. Docker only warns about an unused build argument, so the job can be updated first.

*Testing*
These runs come from a trial GitHub Actions workflow in my fork; that workflow is not part of this change. GitHub keeps their logs for 90 days. Sizes here are in decimal GB; the run summaries print GiB.
* [Fork run 42493777552|https://github.com/GauthamBanasandra/hadoop/actions/runs/42493777552] tested this change; since then only comments and a Linux-cache path filter have changed. It shows as failed because of its ltsc2019 job, explained below. The default (ltsc2022) image built on windows-2022: 16.9 GB, 6.6 GB compressed (15.75 and 6.13 GiB in the run summary). It then passed full {{\-Pnative-win}} builds (120/120 modules, with {{\-DskipTests}}) and a native smoke test ({{TestHdfsNativeCodeLoader}} with {{\-Drequire.test.libhadoop}}) on windows-2022 and windows-2025 under process isolation, and on windows-2022 under Hyper-V isolation.
* The Windows-specific unit tests ran on windows-2022 only: 12 classes in hadoop-common, hadoop-hdfs and hadoop-yarn-common, 275 tests, no failures, 33 skipped. That run excluded six methods that fail both on windows-2022 and in Jenkins nightly #1470 (this change does not exclude them): {{TestFileUtil#testUnZip}}, {{#testFailFullyDeleteDirSymlinks}}, {{#testSymlinkSameFile}} and {{#testGetDU}}, {{TestNativeIO#testFstat}}, and {{TestFsShellCopy#testPutSrcFileNoPerm}} (HADOOP-19599).
* In the same run, the ltsc2019 image built under Hyper-V on windows-2022 (10.0.17763.9378, 16.0 GB) and its entry point ran. That job shows as failed only because the fork workflow did not clear the expected exit code 3 of its entry point check: {{docker build}} exited 0, and the log shows "The entry point returned 3 (expected 3)". This ltsc2019 image was not put through a full build. On trunk, the Jenkins nightly is the only CI job that builds the ltsc2019 path, and by 12 November none of its runs since HADOOP-20031 (#1470 to #1481) had completed a full build. #1470 built the image and 117 of the 120 modules, but failed to compile hadoop-yarn-applications-catalog-webapp ({{\-endorseddirs}} cannot be used with {{\--release}}). #1471 and #1475 to #1479 stopped in {{docker build}} (agent out of disk, layer errors). #1472 to #1474, #1480 and #1481 had not started (agents offline).
* [Fork run 43083636020|https://github.com/GauthamBanasandra/hadoop/actions/runs/43083636020] started the 10 November ltsc2022 base (10.0.20348.5870) under process isolation (a {{cmd /c exit 3}} probe) on three windows-2022 hosts still at 10.0.20348.5773, and on a windows-2025 host. Earlier runs built Hadoop under process isolation from the older 5761 base on 5773 and windows-2025 hosts. This agrees with Microsoft's documentation that from Windows Server 2019 on, the base need not match the host's revision, though only a base older than the host has been through a full build.

   [HADOOP-20087](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HADOOP-20087). `dev-support/docker/Dockerfile_windows_10`
   builds from `servercore:ltsc2019` by tag, and the tag moves with every monthly update. GitHub's
   windows-2022 and windows-2025 runners can run ltsc2019 only under Hyper-V isolation. In fork runs,
   Hyper-V isolation made the Maven build 1.07x to 1.46x slower than process isolation, depending on
   the runner's VM type. This prepares the image for a GitHub Actions Windows build (HADOOP-19857):
   
   - **Base:** a build argument, defaulting to `servercore:ltsc2022` pinned by digest
     (10.0.20348.5761, the base the fork runs below tested), so the default base changes only when
     the Dockerfile does. The Dockerfile notes to bump the digest monthly, no sooner than 7 days after
     Microsoft publishes the image (SECURITY.md requires a cooldown; `.github/dependabot.yml` uses 7 days).
   - **Visual Studio Build Tools:** check that `vcvars64.bat` runs, `cl.exe` is found and Windows SDK
     10.0.19041 is present. Today the install step passes even when the installer fails: `start /w`
     reports success to `||` whatever the installer returns (it only sets `%ERRORLEVEL%`), so its
     `IF "%ERRORLEVEL%"=="3010"` test never runs.
   - **vcpkg:** delete the build trees, downloads and packages in the same layer as the install, and turn
     off the binary cache, which kept a second copy of every package. The image shrinks from about
     24.4 GB to 16.9 GB, and from about 8.8 GB to 6.6 GB compressed. Recent runs of the Jenkins Windows
     nightly (#1471, #1477 to #1479) failed in `docker build` with "There is not enough space on the disk".
   - **`C:\tmp`:** created, writable by the Users group. Tests that use `file:///tmp` resolve it to
     `C:\tmp`; on a host without it, `TestPathData#testWithStringAndConfForBuggyPath` fails.
   - **`dev-support/bin/hadoop.sh`:** passes `-Dwindows.cmake.prefix.path`, the property
     hadoop-hdfs-native-client reads, instead of `-Dcmake.prefix.path`. This affects only the Yetus
     build that the Jenkins Windows jobs run.
   - **`build_image_cache.yml`:** changes to the Windows Dockerfile and `dev-support/docker/vcpkg` no
     longer rebuild the Linux image caches. No Linux Dockerfile reads them.
   - **BUILDING.txt:** which hosts need the ltsc2019 build argument, Docker Engine on Windows Server,
     which isolation to use on client and server hosts, when `-m 8g` is needed, and the image size.
   
   #### Behaviour change, and a step before merging
   
   Building without the `WINDOWS_BASE_IMAGE` build argument now needs a Windows 11 or Windows Server
   2022 (or newer) host. Windows 10 and Windows Server 2019 hosts pass
   `--build-arg WINDOWS_BASE_IMAGE=mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2019` and keep following
   that tag, as before; `dev-support/jenkinsfile-windows-10` now passes it.
   
   The Jenkins nightly `hadoop-qbt-trunk-java8-win10-x86_64` keeps its pipeline script in the job
   configuration rather than reading `jenkinsfile-windows-10`, so the same argument has to be added to
   its `docker build` **before this is merged**, or the nightly switches to the ltsc2022 base. Docker
   only warns about an unused build argument, so the job can be updated first. I have the updated
   job script ready; ci-hadoop.apache.org has been unreachable since 12 November, so it is not
   applied yet.
   
   ### How was this patch tested?
   
   In my fork, with a trial GitHub Actions workflow that is not part of this change. GitHub keeps the
   logs for 90 days. Sizes here are in decimal GB; the run summaries print GiB.
   
   - [Fork run 42493777552](https://github.com/GauthamBanasandra/hadoop/actions/runs/42493777552)
     tested this change; since then only comments and a Linux-cache path filter have changed. It shows
     as failed because of its ltsc2019 job, explained below.
     - The default (ltsc2022) image built on windows-2022: 16.9 GB, 6.6 GB compressed (15.75 and
       6.13 GiB in the run summary).
     - It then passed full `-Pnative-win` builds (120/120 modules, with `-DskipTests`) and a native
       smoke test (`TestHdfsNativeCodeLoader` with `-Drequire.test.libhadoop`) on windows-2022 and
       windows-2025 under process isolation, and on windows-2022 under Hyper-V isolation.
     - The Windows-specific unit tests ran on windows-2022 only: 12 classes in hadoop-common,
       hadoop-hdfs and hadoop-yarn-common, 275 tests, no failures, 33 skipped. The run excluded six
       methods that fail both on windows-2022 and in Jenkins nightly #1470 (this change does not exclude
       them): `TestFileUtil#testUnZip`, `#testFailFullyDeleteDirSymlinks`, `#testSymlinkSameFile` and
       `#testGetDU`, `TestNativeIO#testFstat`, and `TestFsShellCopy#testPutSrcFileNoPerm` (HADOOP-19599).
     - The ltsc2019 image built under Hyper-V on windows-2022 (10.0.17763.9378, 16.0 GB) and its entry
       point ran. That job shows as failed only because the fork workflow did not clear the expected
       exit code 3 of its entry point check: `docker build` exited 0, and the log shows "The entry point
       returned 3 (expected 3)". This ltsc2019 image was not put through a full build.
   - On trunk, the Jenkins nightly is the only CI job that builds the ltsc2019 path, and by 12 November
     none of its runs since HADOOP-20031 (#1470 to #1481) had completed a full build. #1470 built the
     image and 117 of the 120 modules, but failed to compile hadoop-yarn-applications-catalog-webapp
     (`-endorseddirs` cannot be used with `--release`).
   - [Fork run 43083636020](https://github.com/GauthamBanasandra/hadoop/actions/runs/43083636020) started
     the 10 November ltsc2022 base (10.0.20348.5870) under process isolation on three windows-2022 hosts
     still at 10.0.20348.5773, and on a windows-2025 host. Earlier runs built Hadoop under process
     isolation from the older 5761 base on newer hosts. This agrees with Microsoft's documentation that
     from Windows Server 2019 on, the base need not match the host's revision.

summary: YARN - Exclude third-party Jetty and servlet API from the catalog-webapp and timelineservice-hbase tests
description:
*Scope*:
* hadoop-yarn-applications-catalog-webapp/pom.xml: solr-test-framework already depends on solr-core (where EmbeddedSolrServer and NodeConfig live), so drop the direct solr-core declaration and keep solr-test-framework (test scope) as the only Solr test dependency. It carries the single exclusion list of Solr's own Jetty modules and servlet API: jetty-io, jetty-xml, jetty-http, jetty-client, jetty-alpn-client, jetty-alpn-java-client, jetty-alpn-server, jetty-alpn-java-server, jetty-continuation, jetty-deploy, jetty-jmx, jetty-rewrite, jetty-security, jetty-servlets, http2-hpack, http2-client, http2-common, http2-http-client-transport, http2-server, javax.servlet:javax.servlet-api, plus commons-collections and jcl-over-slf4j. A Solr upgrade that adds a Jetty artifact needs one entry (review on PR #8699).
* jetty-alpn-java-client: Solr declares 9.4.44, and the managed 9.4.58 copy won only through Maven's declaration-order tie-break via http2-http-client-transport. Exclude it, as solr-solrj already does.
* hadoop-yarn-server-timelineservice-hbase-tests/pom.xml: on hbase-server and hbase-server:tests (test scope), exclude javax.servlet:javax.servlet-api 3.1.0. HBase's shaded Jetty uses the javax.servlet API, which the module still gets through hadoop-common: today javax.servlet-api 3.1.0, and javax.servlet-api 4.0.1 after HADOOP-19970. hbase-server-2 already excludes it the same way.

*Why*: the catalog-webapp tests reach Solr only through EmbeddedSolrServer, which runs no servlet container. Solr's Jetty (9.4.44) lags Hadoop's managed Jetty, so today the module's test classpath holds two Jetty releases. After this change only ${jetty.version} is left. hbase-server 2.6.3 is the only third-party dependency outside Solr that brings its own servlet API; without the exclusion, timelineservice-hbase-tests would keep a second servlet API jar after HADOOP-19970.

*Impact on Jetty 9*: none. All the changed dependencies are test scope, and catalog-webapp's main code uses only solrj. solr-core 8.11.2 stays on the test classpath through solr-test-framework: dependency:list (test scope) of catalog-webapp gives the same 238 artifacts with the single list as with the exclusions on both Solr artifacts. In timelineservice-hbase-tests the same javax.servlet-api 3.1.0 jar still arrives through hadoop-common until HADOOP-19970.

*Downstream*: none.

*CI*: two modules.

*PR*: https://github.com/apache/hadoop/pull/8890

summary: SFTPInputStream reads one byte per call: override read(byte[], int, int)
description:
{{SFTPInputStream}} overrides only {{read()}}. It does not override {{read(byte[], int, int)}}, so the default implementation from {{java.io.InputStream}} is used, and it calls {{read()}} for every byte.

Because of this, every bulk read from an {{sftp://}} path goes byte by byte: {{IOUtils.copyBytes}}, {{readFully}}, positioned reads, {{BufferedInputStream}}. For each byte there is a synchronized call, the checks for closed stream, EOF and seek, a one-byte read in JSch and a statistics update. The read is CPU-bound and very slow, about 6 MB/s on localhost. A bigger buffer on the caller side does not help, because all wrappers end in the same default method.

This is a regression from HADOOP-14566. In branch-3.2 {{SFTPInputStream}} had {{read(byte[], int, int)}}, which called the JSch stream directly. HADOOP-14566 rewrote the class to support seek, and this method was removed. So all releases since 3.3.1 have the problem, and trunk too.

Fix: add {{read(byte[], int, int)}} again. It passes the whole buffer to the JSch stream and updates {{pos}}, {{nextPos}} and the statistics in the same way as {{read()}}.

Benchmark: sequential read of a 1 GiB file from a local OpenSSH sftp server, with {{FileSystem.open()}} and {{IOUtils.copyBytes()}} with a 64 KB buffer:

||Build||Run 1||Run 2||Run 3||Mean||
|trunk (28c018cdafe)|6.0 MB/s|6.0 MB/s|6.0 MB/s|6.0 MB/s|
|with fix|530.5 MB/s|554.7 MB/s|539.7 MB/s|541.6 MB/s|

Corretto 21.0.13, 16 vCPU. Runs were interleaved: before, after, before, after, ...

I will open a PR with the fix and a unit test.

iatsuk opened a new pull request, #8967:
URL: https://github.com/apache/hadoop/pull/8967

   ### Description of PR
   
   `SFTPInputStream` overrides only `read()`, so bulk reads use the default `InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)` and go to JSch one byte at a time. This method was removed in HADOOP-14566 (seek support).
   
   This PR adds `read(byte[], int, int)` again. It passes the whole buffer to the JSch stream and updates `pos`, `nextPos` and the statistics in the same way as `read()`. The arguments are checked with `validatePositionedReadArgs()` like in `S3AInputStream`. As in `fsdatainputstream.md`, a read with `len == 0` returns 0, and a read at EOF returns -1.
   
   ### How was this patch tested?
   
   - New test `TestSFTPFileSystem#testReadFileInBulk`: reads a 1 MB + 17 bytes random file with 64 KB bulk reads, checks the data, the position, the result at EOF, a backward seek with `readFully()` and the `bytesRead` statistic.
   - `mvn -pl hadoop-common-project/hadoop-common test -Dtest='TestSFTPFileSystem,TestSFTPContractSeek'`: 32 tests, no failures. `TestSFTPContractSeek` is important here, because `readFully()` and positioned reads now use the new method.
   
   Benchmark: sequential read of a 1 GiB file (from `/dev/urandom`) from a local OpenSSH sftp server, with `FileSystem.open()` and `IOUtils.copyBytes(in, OutputStream.nullOutputStream(), 65536, false)`. Corretto 21.0.13, 16 vCPU, runs were interleaved.
   
   | Build | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Mean |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | trunk (28c018cdafe) | 6.0 MB/s | 6.0 MB/s | 6.0 MB/s | 6.0 MB/s |
   | this PR | 530.5 MB/s | 554.7 MB/s | 539.7 MB/s | 541.6 MB/s |
   
   The SHA-256 of the data read with the fix is the same as the SHA-256 of the file.

summary: ZKDelegationTokenSecretManager startup cache load races with CuratorCache initialization
comments:
pan3793 opened a new pull request, #8688:
URL: https://github.com/apache/hadoop/pull/8688

   ### Description of PR
   
   ZKDelegationTokenSecretManager reads the CuratorCache immediately after
   starting it, but CuratorCache populates asynchronously, so the cache can
   still be empty and existing tokens/keys are silently not loaded into memory
   on startup. It also created the root container znodes data-less, which
   Curator 5.2.0+ defaults to the local address, so the container znode data
   could not be parsed.
   
   This change:
   - Waits for CuratorCache initialization (forInitialized) before loading each cache.
   - Skips the root container znode (/ZKDTSMMasterKeyRoot, /ZKDTSMTokensRoot)
     when processing cache events and when streaming the cache, since it is a
     container rather than a key/token.
   - Creates the root container znodes with explicit empty data.
   - Restores the thread-local curator and closes the client in the tests that
     use setCurator, and waits for the good token to load in
     testNodesLoadedAfterRestart.
   
   Contains content generated by deepseek-v4-pro
   
   ### How was this patch tested?
   
   mvn -pl hadoop-common-project/hadoop-common -am \
     -Dtest=TestZKDelegationTokenSecretManager test

   Also there is a race that needs to be solved:
   
   **The race**
   
   After `awaitCacheInitialized(...)`, `loadFromZKCache()` applies a snapshot of every cached node on the thread calling `startThreads()`. By then the cache listener is already applying newer events on Curator's `SafeNotifyService` thread. Nothing orders the two, so the starting thread can apply an older snapshot of a token after the listener has applied a newer state:
   
   ```
   starting thread                        listener thread
   reads cached DT_n (valid)
                                          peer cancels DT_n
                                          NODE_DELETED -> currentTokens.remove(DT_n)
   processTokenAddOrUpdate(old bytes)
     -> currentTokens.put(DT_n)           (nothing removes it again)
   ```
   
   Effects on the instance that is starting:
   - A token cancelled by a peer during startup goes back into memory, and `verifyToken()` **accepts it** until it is renewed or reaches its renew date.
   - A token renewed by a peer during startup gets its **old renew date** back in memory, so this instance's expiry scan can later delete a token that is still valid in ZooKeeper.
   
   Trunk does not have this race. There, `loadFromZKCache()` reads the cache before it is filled (the bug this PR fixes), so the starting thread never applies a token and the listener applies everything in order.
   
   **Evidence**
   
   The same test runs unchanged on trunk and on this PR. A peer cancels 300 tokens while another instance starts; afterwards, none of them may be in the restarted instance's memory or pass `verifyToken()`. The only timing aid is a 2 ms sleep whenever the starting thread applies a token itself, which does nothing on trunk.
   
   | Version | Runs | Failed | Tokens applied by the starting thread | Cancelled tokens still accepted |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | trunk `57f78d2` | 13 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
   | this PR `ccf5b7f` | 13 | 6 | 170–209 | 1–3 per failed run |
   
   Two deterministic tests reproduce the cancel and the renew cases one at a time. They pause the starting thread before it applies a token, let a real peer change it, and use a `runSafe()` no-op as a barrier until the listener has handled the change. In Curator 5.2.0, listener calls and `runSafe()` tasks run in order on one thread. Tests and write-up:
   https://github.com/joseluisll/hadoop/blob/zkdtsm-race-repro/ZKDTSM-RACES-REPORT.md (section 5)
   
   **Suggested fix (tested)**
   
   Drop `loadFromZKCache()` and let the listener apply the initial nodes too: no `.afterInitialized()`, and after the await only `syncTokenOwnerStats()` for the token cache. Curator delivers the initial nodes, then later changes, then `initialized()`, all in order on one thread. So when the latch opens, memory is complete and no older snapshot can land afterwards. With this change all 13 tests in `TestZKDelegationTokenSecretManager` pass, including `testNodesLoadedAfterRestart` with its immediate assertion.

summary: HADOOP - Remove the duplicate javax.annotation-api from the classpath
description:
*Scope*:
* hadoop-project/pom.xml: on javax-websocket-server-impl, exclude javax.annotation:javax.annotation-api, which arrives through jetty-annotations. jakarta.annotation-api 1.3.5 already provides the same javax.annotation classes.
* LICENSE-binary and NOTICE-binary: replace javax.annotation:javax.annotation-api:1.3.2 with jakarta.annotation:jakarta.annotation-api:1.3.5. The jakarta jar is already bundled (through jersey-common) but is missing from LICENSE-binary.
* hadoop-yarn-server-nodemanager: add TestAnnotationApiClasspath, which checks that javax/annotation/PostConstruct.class comes from exactly one jar, jakarta.annotation-api. With trunk's poms it fails: both jars provide the class. It is self-contained and does not depend on HADOOP-19970.

*Why*: two jars publish the javax.annotation packages, and which one a module sees depends on jar order.

*Impact on Jetty 9*: none. Same classes.

*Downstream*:
* hadoop-yarn-server-nodemanager, the only module that declares javax-websocket-server-impl: its consumers no longer get javax.annotation-api 1.3.2. jakarta.annotation-api 1.3.5 provides the same javax.annotation classes.
* hadoop-client-minicluster: loses its relocated copy of javax.annotation-api and keeps the relocated jakarta.annotation-api. Not API.
* hadoop-client-api, hadoop-client-runtime: unchanged.

*CI*: touches hadoop-project, so a full build.

*PR*: https://github.com/apache/hadoop/pull/8891

   - The `root`/`.` module is scheduled only because `LICENSE-binary` and `NOTICE-binary` sit at the repo root, which pulls in a whole-reactor SpotBugs run (`modules: C: hadoop-project ... . U: .`).
   
   Where the 80 come from — modules that inherit SpotBugs from the root pom without wiring in `dev-support/findbugs-exclude-global.xml`:
   
   | module | warnings |
   |---|---|
   | hadoop-tools/hadoop-distcp | 21 |

   78 of the 80 are patterns the global filter already lists (`EI_EXPOSE_REP`/`REP2`, `CT_CONSTRUCTOR_THROW`, `AT_STALE_THREAD_WRITE_OF_PRIMITIVE`, `SS_SHOULD_BE_STATIC`, ...). They surface only because those poms never reference the filter that HADOOP-19731 added; `hadoop-rumen` is the one module here that does have a local filter, and its single warning is a pattern neither filter lists. Hadoop uses {{pull_request_target}} to put the "Build" check on pull requests. Contributors run {{build_and_test.yml}} in their own fork on {{push}}, and two upstream workflows mirror that run onto the PR:
* {{notify_test_workflow.yml}} ({{pull_request_target}}) finds the fork's run and creates the "Build" check.
* {{update_build_status.yml}} (cron, every 15 minutes) updates the check until the fork run completes.

Once the trigger is disabled, PRs lose the "Build" check.

h3. Proposal

Replace both workflows with one schedule-driven bridge built on ASF Infra's [fork-ci action|https://github.com/apache/infrastructure-actions/tree/fork-ci/v1.0.0/fork-ci] ({{fork-ci/v1.0.0}}):
* Add {{.github/workflows/fork_ci_status.yml}}. It is triggered only by {{schedule}} (every 10 minutes) and {{workflow_dispatch}}. It has no {{pull_request_target}} and no {{workflow_run}} trigger, which SECURITY.md disallows and zizmor flags as a dangerous trigger.
* The job token has only {{actions: read}}, {{checks: write}} and {{pull-requests: read}}. The workflow is guarded to {{apache/hadoop}}, serialized in one concurrency group, and runs on {{ubuntu-slim}} with a 10-minute timeout. The action is pinned by commit SHA.
* fork-ci reads GitHub API metadata only. It never checks out, builds or downloads anything from the PR or the fork, and it writes only its own checks.
* Keep the check name "Build". Mirror PRs against {{trunk}}, the only branch that currently has {{build_and_test.yml}}.
* Add {{workflow_dispatch}} to {{build_and_test.yml}}, as fork-ci requires. Contributors can then rerun the build on their PR branch without pushing again.
* Delete {{notify_test_workflow.yml}} and {{update_build_status.yml}} in the same change, so two bridges never write "Build" checks at the same time.
* Update {{.github/workflow-security.md}} to describe the new bridge and the {{schedule}} / {{workflow_dispatch}} triggers.

h3. Behaviour changes for contributors

* A new PR's "Build" check appears on the next scheduled run, typically within 10-20 minutes, instead of right after the PR is opened.
* If no fork run is found, the check is now "neutral" with setup advice instead of "action required". Disabled fork workflows still get "action required".
* On PRs that are open at the cutover, the old "Build" check stops updating, and a new "Build" check appears beside it until the next push.

h3. Out of scope (follow-ups)

* {{labeler.yml}} and {{notify_cloud_aws.yml}} also use {{pull_request_target}} and need their own migration before the cutoff.
* A "Build (Windows)" check for the planned {{build_and_test_windows.yml}} can be added later as a second fork-ci step in the same workflow.

GauthamBanasandra opened a new pull request, #8912:
URL: https://github.com/apache/hadoop/pull/8912

   ### Description of PR
   
   ASF Infra disables `pull_request_target` for ASF repositories from November 2026
   (https://infra.apache.org/github-actions-policy.html). Hadoop uses it to create the "Build" check
   on PRs, which mirrors the contributor's fork run of `build_and_test.yml`:
   
   - `notify_test_workflow.yml` (`pull_request_target`) finds the fork's push run and creates the check.
   - `update_build_status.yml` (cron every 15 minutes) PATCHes it until the run completes.
   
   Without a replacement, PRs lose the "Build" check. This PR replaces both workflows with
   `fork_ci_status.yml`, which calls ASF Infra's
   [fork-ci](https://github.com/apache/infrastructure-actions/tree/fork-ci/v1.0.0/fork-ci) action
   (`fork-ci/v1.0.0`, pinned to `36e391618baf31f50c5a7a7347faf00cba6cf085`):
   
   - **Triggers:** `schedule` every 10 minutes on odd minutes (`7,17,...,57`) plus `workflow_dispatch`.
     There is no `pull_request_target`, and no `workflow_run` either: SECURITY.md disallows it and
     zizmor flags it (`dangerous-triggers`). The cost is latency. A new PR's check appears on the next
     scheduled run (typically within 10-20 minutes, since GitHub often delays scheduled runs) rather
     than within seconds of opening the PR.
   - **Token:** job-level `actions: read`, `checks: write`, `pull-requests: read`; workflow-level
     `permissions: {}`. fork-ci reads API metadata only. It never checks out, builds or downloads
     anything from the PR or fork.
   - **Scope:** guarded by `github.repository == 'apache/hadoop'`, one serialized concurrency group
     (`cancel-in-progress: false`), `ubuntu-slim`, 10-minute timeout.
   - **Branches:** `base-branches: trunk`. Today trunk is the only branch with `build_and_test.yml`;
     branch-3.3.x, 3.4.x and 3.5.x do not have it. Add a release branch only after the workflow lands there.
   - `build_and_test.yml` gains `workflow_dispatch:` as fork-ci asks. A contributor can then rerun the
     build on their PR branch from their fork's Actions tab without pushing again, and fork-ci mirrors
     that run too.
   - `.github/workflow-security.md` notes the `pull_request_target` removal, documents the
     `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch` triggers and describes the new bridge.
   
   The two old workflows are deleted in this same PR so that two bridges never write "Build" checks at
   the same time.
   
   #### Check name: kept as "Build"
   
   - **For "Build":** contributors and committers already look for this name. "Build (Windows)" (planned
     for `build_and_test_windows.yml`) reads as its sibling. Nothing gates merges on it, because
     `.asf.yaml` has no required status checks.
   - **Against "Build":** PRs that are open at cutover keep their legacy "Build" check, which is no
     longer updated, beside fork-ci's new "Build" check until the next push. fork-ci never adopts or
     overwrites the legacy check: it only updates checks whose `external_id` it set itself
     (`fork-ci:build_and_test.yml:pr:<n>`).
   - **"Build (fork)"** would avoid that same-name overlap and put "contributor-controlled" in the name.
     But fork-ci already says that in every check summary, and the overlap disappears on the next push.
     Per the fork-ci README, renaming later creates a new check and leaves the old one behind, so it is
     better to decide now.
   
   #### API budget
   
   Today's `update_build_status.yml` checks every open PR on each run. Run 41221515991 covered 287
   PRs and sent ~169 PATCHes: about 630 REST calls per run, ~2,500 per hour. It succeeds, so the
   repository's `GITHUB_TOKEN` limit is above that. fork-ci lists all open PRs (3 pages for ~285)
   but polls only a rotating group of 25 plus PRs updated in the last 6 hours: roughly 100-150 calls
   per run, ~600-900 per hour at 6 runs per hour. A full rotation over ~280 trunk PRs takes about 2 hours.
   
   #### Follow-ups (not in this PR)
   
   - `labeler.yml` (`pull_request_target`, unpinned `actions/checkout@v3`, `actions/labeler@v4.3.0`) and
     `notify_cloud_aws.yml` (`pull_request_target`) must also be migrated before the cutoff.
   - `build_and_test_windows.yml` / "Build (Windows)": add a second fork-ci step to `fork_ci_status.yml`
     with its own `workflow`, `check-name` and `base-branches`, plus `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`.
   - `.github/workflows/images/workflow-enable-button.png` is now unused. Legacy "action_required"
     checks still embed its raw trunk URL, so it is left in place for now.
   
   ### How was this patch tested?
   
   - actionlint 1.7.12: no findings in the changed workflows.
   - zizmor 1.31.1, default persona with online audits (impostor-commit, ref-confusion, etc. via the
     GitHub API): `fork_ci_status.yml` has no findings, and it is also clean under `--persona=pedantic`.
     The only findings in `build_and_test.yml` are three pre-existing `self-repository` help notes on
     unchanged lines, identical to trunk. Repo-wide, findings drop from 125 to 116 (37 → 34 high),
     because the deleted workflows used `pull_request_target` and unpinned `actions/github-script@v9`.
   - Checked that `apache/*` actions are implicitly trusted by `allowlist-check`, which
     `asf_allowlist_check.yml` (HADOOP-20050, #8906) runs on this PR. fork-ci's nested
     `actions/github-script@3a2844b7…` is the same pin Hadoop already uses.
   - Not exercised live. The bridge only acts on PRs into apache/hadoop from other repositories, so it
     cannot run in a contributor fork as-is. After merge, a committer should run
     `gh workflow run fork_ci_status.yml -R apache/hadoop` and confirm that a "Build" check with a
     "Fork run …" title and a link to the fork run appears on a recently pushed PR. Then confirm that a
     PR from a fork with Actions disabled gets "action_required" with setup advice. The check is
     informational, so reverting this PR is a safe rollback.
   
   ### For code changes:
   
   - [x] Does the title of this PR start with the corresponding JIRA issue id (e.g. 'HADOOP-17799. Your PR title ...')?
   - [ ] Object storage: N/A
   - [ ] New dependencies: none (fork-ci is an ASF Infra action)
   - [ ] LICENSE/NOTICE: N/A
   
   ### AI Tooling
   
   - [x] The PR includes the phrase "Contains content generated by Claude Code"

   Unlike `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch` runs the ref selected by the dispatcher, as `.github/workflow-security.md:145-147` also explains. There is no default-branch guard here, so this workflow does not always run code from the default branch. Please distinguish the two triggers in this security comment rather than implying a restriction that is not enforced.

 Since they are privileged, though, you must be careful not to run untrusted
 code or depend on untrusted variables.

+
+***privileged***
+
+`schedule` events run the workflow from the latest commit on the default
+branch. `workflow_dispatch` events run it on a branch chosen by the user who

+cannot trigger either of them, so the workflow code that runs has been

Review Comment:
   Not being PR-triggerable does not guarantee that the selected code has been reviewed: a user with write access can manually dispatch an unreviewed branch. Please describe the write-access trust boundary without asserting code review, so this guidance does not imply that `workflow_dispatch` enforces a review requirement.

   Thanks for the thorough review. Changes in 4c63885f8, and the PR description is updated:
   
   1. Agreed. I spot-checked forks whose legacy check is `action_required`: their workflow lookup returned 404 or `active`, never `disabled_*`. The description now says no-run PRs get `neutral`. The post-merge step now expects a `neutral` "No fork run for this commit" check that links to the guide. Raising the 404 case with Infra is listed as a follow-up.
   2. Set `sweep-size: "50"`. That gives about a one-hour rotation over the ~264 eligible PRs at roughly 1,000 calls per hour.
   3. Added `.github/pr-build-check.md` and set `guide-url` to it. It covers enabling Actions, rebasing onto trunk, what a no-run check means, and how to rerun, and it reuses the existing enable-button image.
   4. I kept the SHA pin. SECURITY.md requires actions to be pinned by commit SHA, and zizmor reports `fork-ci@fork-ci/v1` as `unpinned-uses` (error). The Dependabot config from HADOOP-20050 now proposes the bumps, so fixes still arrive without hand-written bump PRs. Happy to revisit if we relax the policy for `apache/*` actions.

   6. Noted in the description as deliberate upstream behaviour, and listed as something to raise with Infra.
   7. Reworded in the workflow comment, `workflow-security.md` and the description. Leaving out `workflow_run` is now described as our choice, with the reasons.
   8. Noted in the description: the 46 same-repository PRs (45 from Dependabot) lose the mirrored check and keep their native `Run / ...` checks.
   9. Noted in the description.

   ### Description of PR
   
   Addendum to HADOOP-20056 (#8912): bump the fork-ci pin in `.github/workflows/fork_ci_status.yml` from v1.0.0 to v1.0.1, along with the README link in the header comment. Nothing else changes.
   
   fork-ci v1.0.1 is the merge of apache/infrastructure-actions#1514, which fixes apache/infrastructure-actions#1512. GitHub stores a check's own page as its `details_url`, not the fork-run link the bridge sends, so on v1.0.0 the "unchanged, skip the write" comparison never matches. As a result, every sweep re-reads the PR and rewrites its check. v1.0.1 leaves `details_url` out of that comparison. The run link is still compared through `summary`, so a new run still gets written.
   
   On trunk today, the last four scheduled sweeps wrote 58 of 68, 51 of 61, 42 of 51 and 56 of 71 checks ([43591051145](https://github.com/apache/hadoop/actions/runs/43591051145), [43591852730](https://github.com/apache/hadoop/actions/runs/43591852730), [43592537736](https://github.com/apache/hadoop/actions/runs/43592537736), [43594106711](https://github.com/apache/hadoop/actions/runs/43594106711)). The bridge sweeps 6 times an hour.
   
   The plan in #8912 was for Dependabot (HADOOP-20050) to propose this bump. With the 7-day cooldown and a weekly schedule, that would come around 2026-11-21 at the earliest, inside the grouped github-actions PR (#8911 is currently open with eight major-version bumps). cxzl25 opened a new pull request, #8962:
URL: https://github.com/apache/hadoop/pull/8962

   ### Description of PR
   `TestRegistryDNS#testMissingReverseLookup` (and `TestSecureRegistryDNS`, which extends it) expects `NXDOMAIN` for the unregistered PTR record `19.1.17.172.in-addr.arpa.`, but fails on some CI runners with:
   ```
   AssertionFailedError: Missing record should be:  ==> expected: <3> but was: <0>
   ```
   
   When `RegistryDNS#generateReply` can't answer a name from its own zones, it forwards the query through `remoteLookup` → `getRecords` → `LookupTask`, which is a real dnsjava `Lookup` against the host's resolvers. So the result depends on the environment:
   
   - upstream has no answer → `Lookup` returns `null` → NPE caught → `NXDOMAIN` (passes)
   - upstream answers the PTR → records added → `NOERROR` (fails)
   
   `172.17.0.0/16` is Docker's default bridge network, and the GitHub Actions jobs run inside Docker containers, so the upstream resolver there may answer PTR queries for that range.
   
   This PR changes only the test. It overrides `getRecords()` to return `null`, which simulates an upstream that has no answer, so the test checks only RegistryDNS's own handling of a missing reverse record. No production code changes.
   
   ### How was this patch tested?
   `TestRegistryDNS` and `TestSecureRegistryDNS` pass locally

summary: S3A: default analytics input stream keeps per-object state for the life of the filesystem, so heap grows unbounded in long-running processes
description:
Since HADOOP-19559 (3.4.3, 3.5.0), the default value of {{fs.s3a.input.stream.type}} changed from {{classic}} to {{analytics}}. As a result, each {{S3AFileSystem}} reads through an analyticsaccelerator-s3 {{BlobStore}}. In the library version Hadoop ships (1.3.1), that store keeps an entry for every distinct object read until the filesystem is closed: its periodic cleanup frees the cached data, but not the entries.

With the filesystem cache, an S3A filesystem typically lives as long as the process, so a long-running service that keeps reading new objects grows its heap without limit. Short-lived jobs don't notice because the filesystem is discarded at exit.

The library issue, with a library-only reproduction, is [https://github.com/awslabs/analytics-accelerator-s3/issues/371], and a proposed fix is [https://github.com/awslabs/analytics-accelerator-s3/pull/372].

h3. Which reads are affected

Not every read leaves an entry. The library chooses how to handle each stream from the file name and the read policy, and streams it handles as sequential remove their entry when closed. So it depends on the file type and how the file is opened:

||Read||Entry left after close||
|{{.avro}}, plain {{FileSystem.open()}}|yes|
|{{.parquet}}, plain {{FileSystem.open()}}|yes|
|{{.json}} (also {{.csv}}, {{.txt}}), plain {{FileSystem.open()}}|no|
|{{.avro}}, {{openFile()}} with read policy {{sequential}} or {{whole-file}}|no|
|{{.avro}}, with {{fs.s3a.experimental.input.fadvise=sequential}}|no|

The attached project tests each row; {{.csv}}, {{.txt}} and {{whole-file}} are from the library's {{ObjectFormatSelector}} and {{AnalyticsStream}}'s read-policy mapping rather than tested.

So a plain {{open()}} of a non-text file builds up, which is the common case. For example, Apache Iceberg's {{HadoopInputFile}} uses a plain {{fs.open(path)}}, so every Avro manifest and manifest list read through HadoopFileIO on S3A leaves an entry, while its {{.metadata.json}} files don't. That is how we found it: a long-running Iceberg replication service ran out of a 160 MB heap after about 1,000 table commits.

h3. Reproduction through S3A

The attached Gradle project reproduces it through a Hadoop 3.5.0 {{S3AFileSystem}} with default settings, using hadoop-aws's own {{AbstractS3AMockTest}} and {{MockS3ClientFactory}}, so no endpoint is needed ({{./gradlew test}}, about 30 seconds, Java 17). Every stream is opened, read fully and closed.

||Check||Result||
|Entries after reading 2,000 distinct .avro objects (4 KB each)|2,000|
|After re-reading 1,000 of them|still 2,000 (one entry per distinct object)|
|12 seconds later, no reads|still 2,000|
|After reading 6,000 distinct objects|6,000, no limit reached|
|Heap held with the filesystem open|about 31 KB per object read|
|Heap held after {{fs.close()}}|back to the starting level|
|Same reads with {{fs.s3a.input.stream.type=classic}}|about 80 bytes per object|

With a 160 MB heap the default stream ran out of memory after 2,000 to 3,000 distinct objects; with {{classic}} the same 50,000 reads completed.

h3. Workarounds

* {{fs.s3a.input.stream.type=classic}}
* {{fs.s3a.experimental.input.fadvise=sequential}}, at the cost of the analytics stream's format-specific handling

h3. Suggested changes in Hadoop

# Once a fixed analyticsaccelerator-s3 release is available, upgrade to it.
# Documentation: the default change isn't visible to users today.
#* The 3.4.3 and 3.5.0 release notes pages don't mention HADOOP-19559 or the stream type change; the note is only in the JIRA's release-note field.
#* {{hadoop-aws/src/site/markdown/tools/hadoop-aws/reading.md}} in 3.5.0 still lists {{classic}} as the default for {{fs.s3a.input.stream.type}}, while {{StreamIntegration.DEFAULT_STREAM_TYPE}} is {{Analytics}}.
#* Until a fixed library is shipped, it may be worth noting {{classic}} for long-running processes there.

ATTACHMENT:  [^s3a-analytics-blobstore-repro.zip]

summary: RawLocalFileSystem: broken double-checked locking in LocalFSFileInputStream#getAsyncChannel() can leak AsynchronousFileChannels
description:
LocalFSFileInputStream#getAsyncChannel() checks {{asyncChannel == null}} outside the lock but not again inside it, and the field is not volatile. When two threads make the first readVectored() call on the same stream, both can open an AsynchronousFileChannel. The last assignment wins and close() only closes that channel, so the other one keeps its file descriptor open until the JVM exits. PositionedReadable requires positioned reads, readVectored included, to be thread-safe.

The fix makes the field volatile and checks it again inside the synchronized block. This was pointed out in the review of HADOOP-19901: https://github.com/apache/hadoop/pull/8511#discussion_r4452981403. A readVectored() call after close() still opens a new channel; this change does not touch that.
comments:
LuciferYang opened a new pull request, #8931:
URL: https://github.com/apache/hadoop/pull/8931

   ### Description of PR
   
   JIRA: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HADOOP-20067
   
   `LocalFSFileInputStream#getAsyncChannel()` checks `asyncChannel == null` outside the lock but not again inside it, and the field is not volatile. When two threads make the first `readVectored()` call on the same stream, both can open an `AsynchronousFileChannel`. `close()` only closes the one left in the field, so the other keeps its file descriptor until the JVM exits. `PositionedReadable` requires positioned reads, `readVectored` included, to be thread-safe.
   
   This patch makes the field volatile and checks it again inside the `synchronized` block. It follows up on https://github.com/apache/hadoop/pull/8511#discussion_r4452981403. A `readVectored()` after `close()` still opens a new channel; that is unchanged here.
   
   ### How was this patch tested?
   
   Added `TestRawLocalFileSystemAsyncChannel#testConcurrentGetAsyncChannelOpensSingleChannel`: eight threads released from a barrier call `getAsyncChannel()` on a fresh stream and must all get the same channel, which must be closed after `close()`. With the fix this is deterministic. Without it the test fails when the threads race, which depends on scheduling, so the race runs three times.
